lessons.title: Laboratory skills and scientific investigation
objectives: Choose apparatus and read measurements appropriately.
Plan a controlled investigation.
Follow laboratory and emergency boundaries.
paragraphs: Chemistry investigates substances, their properties and the changes they undergo. It connects with farming through fertilisers and soils, health through medicines and diagnostics, industry through materials and fuels, and environmental work through water and pollution analysis. A benefit must be considered alongside safe handling and waste disposal; producing a useful substance does not make every use harmless.

A laboratory is a controlled workplace, not a place to taste or casually mix substances. Read instructions before starting, wear the required eye protection and clothing, tie back long hair and keep exits clear. Report broken apparatus, spills and injuries promptly. Never pipette by mouth. Heating, concentrated chemicals, unfamiliar reactions and fire response require a teacher or competent supervisor. In an emergency, alert the responsible adult and follow the school emergency procedure instead of improvising a chemical treatment.

Choose apparatus to match the task. A beaker holds and mixes liquids but is not usually the best instrument for an accurate volume. A measuring cylinder measures liquid volume more closely; a balance measures mass. A funnel supports transfer or filtration, a test tube holds small samples and a thermometer measures temperature. Inspect apparatus for damage and read scales at an appropriate eye level. Where a clear liquid forms a curved surface, the bottom of the meniscus is commonly read at eye level; the instrument and liquid determine the correct convention.

An investigation begins with a clear question and a testable prediction. Change the independent variable, observe or measure the dependent variable, and keep relevant controlled variables similar. Repeat observations to identify variation, record units and distinguish observations from conclusions. A fair test of dissolving rate could vary water temperature while keeping water volume, solute mass, particle size and stirring conditions comparable. A result supports a conclusion only within the tested conditions.
examples: Question: Does temperature affect dissolving time? Independent variable: temperature. Dependent variable: time to dissolve. Controls include water volume and solute amount. Do not change temperature and stirring at the same time.
A beaker suggests about 50 mL while a suitable measuring cylinder allows a finer reading. Choose the cylinder for a volume measurement and a balance if the task asks for mass.
Observation: a solid remains on the filter. Conclusion: an insoluble component was retained. The observation alone does not identify the substance or prove the filtrate is safe to drink.
lessons.summary: Chemistry investigates substances, their properties and the changes they undergo.

lessons.title: Measurements, graphs and experimental evidence
objectives: Select suitable measurement tools.
Calculate and interpret means and ranges.
Present evidence in labelled tables and graphs.
paragraphs: A useful measurement states a quantity, a numerical value and a unit. Select an instrument with a suitable range and resolution: a metre rule for ordinary length, a stopwatch for time, a balance for mass and a measuring cylinder for liquid volume. The smallest scale division influences how finely the result can be read. More decimal digits do not automatically mean a more accurate measurement.

Check zero readings and view scales carefully. A zero error shifts readings even when nothing should register. Parallax results from viewing a scale from the wrong angle. Repeated readings can reveal random variation, but repeating a biased method does not remove systematic error. Record what was actually observed, including an unexpected value; investigate a suspected mistake rather than quietly replacing it.

Organise data in a table with a clear heading and units for each column. The mean is the sum of values divided by their number; the range is maximum minus minimum. Values should be combined only when they describe comparable quantities and conditions. A missing reading is not zero. A large difference between repeats is a reason to examine technique, timing or conditions.

Graphs show relationships. Put the independent variable on the horizontal axis and the dependent variable on the vertical axis unless the task specifies otherwise. Choose convenient scales, label units and plot points accurately. A best-fit line or curve represents the overall pattern rather than forcing every point into a zigzag. The gradient is vertical change divided by horizontal change, with units inherited from both axes. State the limits of what the graph supports; extrapolating far beyond observations can be unreliable.
examples: Time readings 12.1 s, 11.9 s and 12.0 s have mean 36.0/3=12.0 s and range 0.2 s. Retain the unit in both results.
A distance–time line passes through (2 s,6 m) and (6 s,18 m). Gradient=(18−6)/(6−2)=3 m/s, representing speed for that straight section.
A balance reads 2 g when empty. This suggests a zero error; simply averaging many similarly shifted readings will not remove that bias.
lessons.summary: A useful measurement states a quantity, a numerical value and a unit.

lessons.title: Classification, organisms and microscopes
objectives: Use scientific names correctly.
Compare major school-level organism groups.
Calculate magnification and follow observation conventions.
paragraphs: Biology studies living organisms and their processes. Classification groups organisms using selected characteristics so that similarities, differences and relationships can be studied and information communicated. An artificial system may use a few convenient visible traits; a natural system aims to reflect a broader set of relationships. One superficial similarity does not prove close relationship: a bird and an insect both fly but differ in many major features.

Scientific names reduce confusion between local names. In binomial naming, the first word is the genus and begins with a capital letter; the second is the specific epithet and begins with a lower-case letter. Both are written in italics in print or separately underlined when handwritten. Homo sapiens is an example. A species name is the two-word combination, not the second word alone.

The school classification framework in this syllabus includes Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia, with viruses considered separately. Monera includes organisms such as bacteria that lack a membrane-bound nucleus. Protists are diverse; fungi absorb nutrients and do not photosynthesise like green plants. Most familiar plants make food by photosynthesis, while animals ingest organic food. Viruses are not cellular organisms and reproduce only within host cells. Modern classification systems may organise these groups differently, so identify the framework being used.

A microscope makes small structures visible, but good use requires preparation. Begin with low power, place and secure the slide, illuminate appropriately and focus without striking the slide with the objective. Total magnification is eyepiece magnification multiplied by objective magnification. Keep observations separate from assumptions about identity. Draw clear labelled structures actually seen; do not add organelles simply because a textbook diagram includes them. Slides and biological material should be prepared and handled under the required school guidance.
examples: For a 10× eyepiece and 4× objective, total magnification=10×4=40×. Changing to a 10× objective gives 100×.
A wing is not enough to classify an animal as a bird: insects also have wings. Consider body organisation and other features before deciding.
Write Homo sapiens, not homo Sapiens. The genus starts with a capital; the specific epithet starts lower case, and the full name is treated as a two-word unit.
lessons.summary: Biology studies living organisms and their processes.

lessons.title: Simultaneous equations and straight lines
objectives: Solve and check simultaneous equations.
Calculate gradients and line equations.
Interpret graphical solutions and inequalities.
paragraphs: Two simultaneous equations describe conditions that must hold for the same unknowns. A solution pair must satisfy both equations, not just one. Substitution replaces a variable with an equivalent expression from the other equation. Elimination adds or subtracts suitable multiples so one variable cancels. Keep equality by applying the same operation to both sides.

For x+y=11 and x−y=3, adding gives 2x=14, so x=7 and y=4. Check 7+4=11 and 7−4=3. If equations are proportional, they may describe the same line and have infinitely many solution pairs; if they are inconsistent, there is no common solution. Not every pair of linear equations has exactly one solution.

Coordinates (x,y) locate a point using horizontal and vertical positions relative to chosen axes. For a line through distinct points, gradient m=(y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁), provided x₂≠x₁. In y=mx+c, m is gradient and c the vertical-axis intercept. A vertical line has undefined finite gradient in this formula and is written x=a, not y=mx+c with an ordinary numerical m.

To draw a line, choose convenient x values, calculate the corresponding y values and plot at least two points accurately. Their intersection can show a simultaneous solution. The accuracy depends on scale and plotting; use algebra to obtain an exact result when possible. For inequalities, remember to reverse the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number. A solution interval contains many values, not just one number at its boundary.
examples: Solve x+y=9 and x−y=1. Add: 2x=10, x=5; substitute to get y=4. Both equations are satisfied.
For points (1,4) and (3,10), gradient=(10−4)/(3−1)=3. Using y=3x+c and (1,4), c=1, so the line is y=3x+1.
Solve −2x+3>11. Subtract 3: −2x>8; divide by −2 and reverse the inequality: x<−4. For example x=−5 gives 13>11.
lessons.summary: Two simultaneous equations describe conditions that must hold for the same unknowns.

lessons.title: Kusoma kwa uelewa, msamiati na kamusi
objectives: Soma matini na toa majibu yenye ushahidi.
Chagua maana sahihi kwa msaada wa kamusi.
Andika muhtasari na shiriki mazungumzo kwa heshima.
paragraphs: Usomaji wenye uelewa unahusisha kutambua ujumbe mkuu, taarifa saidizi na uhusiano wa mawazo. Kabla ya kusoma, angalia kichwa na kusudi la kazi. Unaposoma, zingatia alama za uandishi na muktadha wa maneno. Kusoma kwa sauti kunahitaji kasi inayoeleweka na kiimbo kinachoendana na tungo, lakini kuigiza sauti bila kuelewa maana hakutoshi.

Soma matini hii asilia: Mwanaidi alikopa kamusi maktabani ili kuandaa maonesho ya darasa. Alipokutana na neno lisilojulikana, hakuchukua maana ya kwanza tu. Alisoma maana tofauti na kuangalia sentensi aliyokuwa akiandika. Baadaye alimwonyesha Baraka rasimu yake. Baraka alipendekeza afafanue maneno mawili ambayo yangeweza kuwachanganya wasikilizaji. Walipomaliza, walirudisha kamusi kwa wakati na kuweka nakala ya maelezo yao kwenye ubao wa darasa.

Kamusi hupanga vidahizo kwa utaratibu maalumu, mara nyingi wa alfabeti. Kidadisi cha neno kinaweza kuonyesha tahajia, aina ya neno, maana zaidi ya moja, mfano wa matumizi na taarifa nyingine. Taarifa hutofautiana kwa aina ya kamusi. Chagua maana inayolingana na muktadha; si kila maana inafaa kila sentensi. Katika mawasiliano ya kidijitali, tumia kamusi au chanzo kinachotambulika badala ya kuamini tafsiri ya kwanza bila kukagua.

Muhtasari wa matini huchagua hoja kuu na kuziunganisha kwa lugha yako bila kuongeza tukio jipya. Katika mazungumzo, sikiliza hadi uelewe hoja kabla ya kujibu, toa nafasi kwa wengine na uliza ufafanuzi kwa heshima. Kumbukumbu fupi zinaweza kusaidia kufuatilia mawazo, lakini zisigeuze maoni ya mtu kuwa ukweli uliothibitishwa. Mazoezi haya yanaweza kufanywa kwa kusoma matini; mazoezi halisi ya kusikiliza yanahitaji sauti au msomaji.
examples: Kwa nini Mwanaidi hakuchukua maana ya kwanza tu? Kwa sababu alitaka maana inayolingana na sentensi na kusudi lake. Jibu linatokana na matini.
Mpangilio wa alfabeti: amani, bahari, darasa, elimu. Linganisha herufi ya kwanza; ikiwa inafanana, endelea kwenye herufi zinazofuata.
Muhtasari: Mwanaidi alitumia kamusi kwa kuzingatia muktadha, akaboresha rasimu kwa msaada wa Baraka na kurudisha kitabu kwa wakati. Hakuna taarifa kwamba alinunua kamusi.
lessons.summary: Usomaji wenye uelewa unahusisha kutambua ujumbe mkuu, taarifa saidizi na uhusiano wa mawazo.

lessons.title: Geography, landforms, water bodies and vegetation
objectives: Distinguish physical and human geography.
Identify major land and water features.
Explain vegetation and people–environment relationships.
paragraphs: Geography studies places, environments and relationships between people and the Earth. Physical geography examines features and processes such as landforms, water and climate; human geography considers activities such as settlement, farming, transport and trade. These branches overlap: a river affects settlement and transport, while land use can affect the river’s water quality. Maps, field observations and photographs help investigate such relationships.

The commonly used seven-continent model names Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, South America and Australia. Different naming conventions may refer to the wider region of Oceania, so state the model being used. The five commonly recognised oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic. Tanzania lies on the eastern side of Africa with a coast on the Indian Ocean. A continent is a large landmass; an ocean is a major body of salt water.

Relief describes variations in the height and shape of the land. A mountain rises prominently above nearby land; a plateau is an elevated area with a relatively broad level surface; a plain has relatively low relief; a valley is an elongated depression. Definitions describe patterns rather than a guarantee that every surface fits one perfect shape. In Tanzania, Mount Kilimanjaro is a prominent mountain and the surrounding lower land has different relief characteristics.

Inland water bodies include lakes, rivers, wetlands and reservoirs. Lake Victoria, Lake Tanganyika and Lake Nyasa/Malawi are major East African lakes shared across national borders. Rivers flow through drainage basins and can connect upstream activities with downstream effects. Vegetation zones reflect interacting influences including rainfall, temperature, soils, altitude, fire and human activity. Forest, woodland, grassland/savanna and sparse dryland vegetation are broad categories; boundaries vary rather than forming identical bands everywhere.

A geographical explanation links a feature to its significance with evidence. Plains may make some transport routes easier, but floods or soft soils can still create difficulties. Mountains can influence rainfall, water sources and tourism, but also bring steep-slope hazards. Treat a benefit or challenge as dependent on place and conditions. During observation, record location, visible features and human activities without entering unsafe water, unstable slopes or restricted land.
examples: A coastal settlement may depend on fishing and transport links. Explaining it well combines a physical setting, human activities and evidence rather than calling it only physical or only human geography.
Classify three features: Mount Kilimanjaro is a mountain, Lake Tanganyika an inland lake and the Indian Ocean a major ocean. They are not interchangeable kinds of water/land feature.

If bare soil appears after vegetation is removed, investigate runoff, slope and rainfall before predicting erosion. The vegetation change is one part of a connected system, not a complete explanation alone.
lessons.summary: Geography studies places, environments and relationships between people and the Earth.

lessons.title: Planning and starting a sole-trader enterprise
objectives: Separate start-up resources from operating needs.
Calculate practical small-business costs.
Use a trial and records to improve decisions.
paragraphs: A business plan explains a proposed enterprise: the customer need, product or service, resources, operations, expected costs and revenue, and risks. Planning does not guarantee success, but it makes assumptions visible so they can be tested. An entrepreneur should distinguish an attractive idea from evidence that enough customers will buy at a workable price.

Calculate start-up needs separately from running costs. A sewing machine bought to begin tailoring is a start-up asset; thread, rent and transport may recur. Working capital supports day-to-day operations while money is tied up in stock or unpaid sales. If all available cash is spent on equipment, a business may be unable to buy the materials needed to use it.

A sole trader can make decisions directly, but personal capacity and resources limit the operation. Check access to skills, time, suppliers, storage and customers. Keep business transactions recorded even when the owner supplies the money. Money taken for personal use is not evidence of a business expense, and cash put in by the owner is not sales revenue.

A small trial helps test demand and practical problems. Specify what will count as evidence, such as the number of paid orders, full cost per item and customer feedback. Review quality, waste and complaints as well as sales totals. Before operating, check the requirements that apply to the location and activity with the responsible authorities; a school exercise is not a licence or a financial promise.
examples: Equipment costs TSh 40,000 and opening materials TSh 15,000. At least TSh 55,000 is needed for those items, before other costs and cash reserves. Counting equipment alone understates the plan.

A trader buys ten items at TSh 700 each and spends TSh 1000 on transport. Total batch cost=8000, so relevant unit cost before other expenses is 800. At a selling price of 1000, 200 per sold item remains before other costs.

A trial sells six of ten products. Record six sales and four remaining items; do not record ten sales merely because ten were produced. Unsold stock and customer comments both inform the next decision.
lessons.summary: A business plan explains a proposed enterprise: the customer need, product or service, resources, operations, expected costs and revenue, and risks.

lessons.title: Urithi, maadili na ushirikiano wa jamii
objectives: Tambua aina na thamani za urithi.
Husisha maadili na utunzaji unaoheshimu watu.
Chunguza fursa na ushirikiano kwa uwajibikaji.
paragraphs: Urithi wa jamii unajumuisha vitu vinavyoonekana kama majengo, maeneo na zana, na mambo yasiyoshikika kama lugha, simulizi, sanaa na maarifa. Urithi hutusaidia kuchunguza maisha ya vizazi vilivyotangulia na kuelewa utambulisho wa sasa. Hata hivyo, maelezo ya urithi yanahitaji ushahidi; simulizi moja au jina la kitu halithibitishi kila dai linalotolewa kuhusu asili yake.

Maadili yanahusiana na namna watu wanavyotathmini matendo na wajibu wao kwa wengine. Uaminifu, uwajibikaji, heshima na ushirikiano vinaweza kusaidia kujenga maisha ya pamoja. Mila zinapotathminiwa, zingatia heshima ya binadamu na haki badala ya kudai kwamba kila desturi ya zamani ilikuwa nzuri au kwamba kila jambo jipya ni bora. Jamii zinaweza kuhifadhi maarifa yenye thamani huku zikirekebisha matendo yenye madhara.

Utunzaji wa urithi unahitaji ushirikiano wa jamii, wataalamu na mamlaka husika. Usichimbe, kuondoa, kuandika juu au kuuza vitu vya kihistoria bila kufuata taratibu zinazotumika. Kupiga picha au kurekodi maarifa ya mtu kunahitaji kuzingatia ridhaa, faragha na masharti yake. Kuhamisha kitu bila rekodi kunaweza kupoteza muktadha unaosaidia kuelewa matumizi na kipindi chake.

Urithi unaweza kusaidia uchumi kupitia ufundi, maonesho, utalii unaowajibika na elimu. Fursa itathminiwe pamoja na manufaa kwa wenye urithi na gharama za kuutunza. Biashara isiwasilishe vitu vipya kama vya kale kwa udanganyifu au kutoa maarifa ya jamii bila heshima. Shughuli za pamoja kama usafi wa mazingira, kujenga huduma na kubadilishana stadi zinaweza kukuza mshikamano na uwezo wa kiuchumi zinapopangwa kwa uwazi na ushiriki wa haki.
examples: Kikundi cha wanafunzi kinaomba ruhusa ya kusaidia kusafisha eneo la urithi na kinafuata maelekezo ya msimamizi. Huu ni ushiriki unaolenga kuhifadhi, si ruhusa ya kuhamisha vitu vya kale.
Mfundi anatengeneza bidhaa mpya kwa kutumia mbinu za jadi. Anaweza kuieleza kama kazi mpya ya ufundi wa jadi, badala ya kudai kwa uongo kwamba ni kitu cha karne zilizopita.
Jamii inapoweka rekodi ya mapato na matumizi ya maonesho, wanachama wanaweza kujadili manufaa na gharama kwa ushahidi. Uwazi husaidia uwajibikaji.
lessons.summary: Urithi wa jamii unajumuisha vitu vinavyoonekana kama majengo, maeneo na zana, na mambo yasiyoshikika kama lugha, simulizi, sanaa na maarifa.

lessons.title: Finding information and writing friendly messages
objectives: Search with clear questions and relevant terms.
Evaluate source cards and vocabulary in context.
Write complete friendly messages and invitations.
paragraphs: Information search begins with a clear question. Choose keywords describing the topic and the kind of information needed rather than typing a very long vague sentence. A search engine helps locate sources; it is not itself proof that a result is correct. Look for the author or institution, date, purpose and evidence. In offline practice, compare prepared source cards and decide which would answer a stated question; no internet connection is needed for that exercise.

Consider two original source cards. Card A: School library notice, issued Monday, says the library will open at 8 a.m. during revision week. Card B: An undated message says someone heard that all school rooms are closed. For the question about library opening time, Card A is more directly relevant and attributable. It can still be checked with the school if circumstances change. A confident tone and a large number of forwarded messages do not replace a named, relevant source.

When learning vocabulary, record the word, its meaning in context and your own example. A word may have more than one meaning: light can refer to illumination or to low weight. A useful vocabulary game pairs words with suitable contexts rather than treating every dictionary meaning as interchangeable. Retelling a story requires a clear sequence; a summary keeps its main events and omits minor detail without inventing an ending.

A friendly letter normally includes the sender’s address where required, date, greeting, message and closing. Its tone should suit the relationship and purpose. A clear invitation states the activity, place, date and time and asks for a response where needed. Follow the stages of planning, drafting, revising and editing. A timetable records activities and times consistently so that it can be followed by someone who did not help write it.
examples: Question: When does the library open during revision week? Useful keywords might be school library revision week opening time. A current school notice is more relevant than an unrelated general article about libraries.
Context contrast: The bag is light means not heavy; the lamp gives light means illumination. Use the sentence to choose a meaning.

Invitation: Dear Asha, Please join our reading group in the library on Friday at 3 p.m. We will discuss a short story. Let me know whether you can come. Best wishes, Neema. The key practical details are present.
lessons.summary: Information search begins with a clear question.

questions.content: Name two areas where chemistry is useful.
questions.answerKey: Agriculture and health; industry or environmental monitoring are also valid.
questions.markingGuide: Link each area to an example. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Which apparatus measures mass?
questions.answerKey: A balance.
questions.markingGuide: A measuring cylinder measures volume. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Which is more suitable for measuring 35 mL: a beaker or measuring cylinder?
questions.answerKey: A suitable measuring cylinder.
questions.markingGuide: Its scale is intended for volume measurement. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: What is the independent variable in a temperature–dissolving investigation?
questions.answerKey: Water temperature.
questions.markingGuide: It is the deliberately changed factor. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: What can be the dependent variable in that investigation?
questions.answerKey: Time taken for the stated amount to dissolve.
questions.markingGuide: Specify a measurable response. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Give two controlled variables for the investigation.
questions.answerKey: Water volume and solute mass; particle size and stirring are also relevant.
questions.markingGuide: Keep other influential conditions similar. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Why repeat observations?
questions.answerKey: To detect variation and improve confidence in the pattern.
questions.markingGuide: Repeats do not justify inventing identical results. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: State one rule about tasting chemicals.
questions.answerKey: Never taste laboratory chemicals.
questions.markingGuide: They are not safe foods. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: What should happen after an injury or serious spill?
questions.answerKey: Alert the responsible adult and follow the school emergency procedure.
questions.markingGuide: Do not improvise chemical first aid. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: State one use of a funnel.
questions.answerKey: Transferring liquids or supporting filtration.
questions.markingGuide: Match the tool to a specific function. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Why must units accompany numerical measurements?
questions.answerKey: They identify the quantity scale and allow interpretation and comparison.
questions.markingGuide: A bare number is incomplete. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Explain the difference between observation and conclusion.
questions.answerKey: An observation records what was seen or measured; a conclusion interprets the evidence.
questions.markingGuide: Give a linked example. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Why should broken glassware not be used?
questions.answerKey: It can break further, leak or injure someone.
questions.markingGuide: Report it for safe handling. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: What is a testable prediction?
questions.answerKey: A statement of an expected outcome that observations can support or challenge.
questions.markingGuide: It must connect to a measurable investigation. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Why does a clear filtrate not prove purity?
questions.answerKey: Dissolved substances may remain even when particles are not visible.
questions.markingGuide: Clarity and chemical purity are different. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Which instrument measures mass?
questions.answerKey: A balance.
questions.markingGuide: Use an instrument matched to the quantity. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: What is meant by instrument range?
questions.answerKey: The span of values it can measure appropriately.
questions.markingGuide: The required reading should fit within that span. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: What is parallax error?
questions.answerKey: A reading error caused by viewing a scale from an unsuitable angle.
questions.markingGuide: Align the eye appropriately. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: A balance reads 3 g when empty. What type of issue is suggested?
questions.answerKey: Zero error.
questions.markingGuide: A consistent offset can bias all readings. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find the mean of 9, 10 and 11 s.
questions.markingGuide: Add 30 and divide by three. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find the range of 4.2, 4.5 and 4.3 cm.
questions.answerKey: 0.3 cm
questions.markingGuide: Maximum minus minimum. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Why is a missing reading different from zero?
questions.answerKey: Missing means unobserved; zero would claim a real measured value.
questions.markingGuide: Do not fabricate data. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Which graph axis commonly shows the independent variable?
questions.answerKey: Horizontal axis.
questions.markingGuide: Label its quantity and unit. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Give the formula for gradient.
questions.answerKey: Change in vertical quantity divided by change in horizontal quantity.
questions.markingGuide: Use two suitable points on the line. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Find gradient from (1 s,2 m) to (5 s,10 m).
questions.answerKey: 2 m/s
questions.markingGuide: (10−2)/(5−1). Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Why use a best-fit line rather than a zigzag through every reading?
questions.answerKey: It describes the overall relationship without treating each random variation as a real change in trend.
questions.markingGuide: The graph should fit the evidence sensibly. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: Can repeated readings alone remove a systematic error?
questions.answerKey: No. The underlying bias needs to be identified and corrected.
questions.markingGuide: Averaging is not a cure for every error. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.

questions.content: What should a table column heading include?
questions.answerKey: The measured quantity and unit.
questions.markingGuide: Place repeated units in the heading where appropriate. Award up to 2 marks for the correct model response with the requested explanation/working; 1 for a correct key idea with an incomplete explanation.
